discovery.question: Rohan and Sohan pool money for a food truck, share recipes, and split profits 60:40 — but never sign anything. Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, are they legally a partnership?
options: Yes — an agreement to run a business and share profits is enough; writing is not mandatory
No — a partnership exists only once a written deed is registered
No — a firm needs at least three partners to be recognised
Yes — but only after they register the firm with the Registrar
discovery.answer: Yes — an agreement to run a business and share profits is enough; writing is not mandatory
discovery.hook: Students assume law demands paperwork; Section 4 only demands agreement, business, profit-sharing and mutual agency — the deed is evidence, not existence.

c12_acc_ch01.mission: Run a two-partner venture and test every 'are we a partnership?' scenario against Section 4 — then draft the deed clauses that protect both partners before a dispute does it for them.
c12_acc_ch01.finale: You can now spot a partnership in the wild and write the deed that keeps it alive. Board questions love the 'is this a partnership?' trap — and future founders live it.
c12_acc_ch01.subtitle: Two friends, one food truck, and the law that decides if they're partners
c12_acc_ch01.intro: Every business you'll ever build or audit starts with one question: what exactly binds these people together?
c12_acc_ch01.goal: Apply Section 4's essential features and design deed clauses for profit-sharing, capital and disputes.

discovery.question: Three partners sharing 3:2:1 admit a new chef for a 1/6 share. How much does each old partner give up?
options: Whatever their agreement says — the sacrificing ratio is decided by the partners, not fixed by law
Exactly 1/18 each — the new share is always divided equally among old partners
Nothing — the new partner's 1/6 is created fresh, not taken from anyone
Always in their old 3:2:1 ratio — the law mandates it
discovery.answer: Whatever their agreement says — the sacrificing ratio is decided by the partners, not fixed by law
discovery.hook: The reflex is to split the new partner's share equally; in reality sacrifice can follow the old ratio, a fixed ratio, or fall on one partner alone — and goodwill payment rides on that choice.

c12_acc_ch02.mission: Negotiate an admission: compute the new ratio under different sacrifice deals, value the firm's goodwill, and decide what the incoming partner must pay for the reputation they're buying into.
c12_acc_ch02.finale: You now control the two numbers every admission hinges on — new ratio and goodwill. Boards test the ratio algebra; real firms test your negotiation.
c12_acc_ch02.subtitle: A new partner walks in — who gives up what, and what is the goodwill worth?
c12_acc_ch02.intro: Admitting a partner rewrites the firm's entire economics in one afternoon — ratio, goodwill, capital.
c12_acc_ch02.goal: Compute new and sacrificing ratios under varied agreements and account for goodwill on admission.

discovery.question: Chirag retires from a firm where Aryan, Bhavya and Chirag shared 3:2:1. The deed says nothing about who inherits his 1/6 share. What does the law assume?
options: The continuing partners gain in their old ratio — Aryan and Bhavya absorb it 3:2
The share is split equally between the two remaining partners
The share lapses — profits are now shared only between two, with no gain computed
The retiring partner chooses who inherits the share in his will
discovery.answer: The continuing partners gain in their old ratio — Aryan and Bhavya absorb it 3:2
discovery.hook: Silence in the deed is itself an answer: absent an explicit deal, the gaining ratio defaults to the old ratio — and that default decides who funds the retiring partner's goodwill.

c12_acc_ch03.mission: Handle a retirement end-to-end: compute the gaining ratio, compensate the outgoing partner's goodwill share through the gainers' capital accounts, and restate the firm's future profit split.
c12_acc_ch03.finale: Retirement is admission run in reverse — and you've now mastered both directions. Boards love gaining-ratio puzzles; real practice hands you the same arithmetic with real money.
c12_acc_ch03.subtitle: One partner exits — who gains his share, and who pays for his goodwill?
c12_acc_ch03.role: Firm accountant managing a partner's exit
c12_acc_ch03.intro: When a partner leaves, the firm doesn't just lose a person — it silently redistributes every future rupee of profit.
c12_acc_ch03.goal: Compute gaining and new ratios and settle the retiring partner's goodwill through capital adjustments.

discovery.question: Sohan retires and Mohan joins the same firm on a fresh agreement. Has the partnership firm been dissolved?
options: No — this is dissolution of partnership; the firm continues under a new agreement
Yes — any change in partners dissolves the firm itself
Yes — retirement always triggers full closure and asset sale
No — because no court order was issued, nothing was dissolved at all
discovery.answer: No — this is dissolution of partnership; the firm continues under a new agreement
discovery.hook: The single most-confused distinction in partnership law: dissolving the *partnership* rewrites the contract while the business runs on; dissolving the *firm* means selling everything and paying everyone off.

c12_acc_ch04.mission: Adjudicate dissolution scenarios — agreement, notice, court order — and decide in each case whether the business survives or the firm must be wound up, assets realised and liabilities cleared.
c12_acc_ch04.finale: You'll never again mix up 'the deal changed' with 'the business died'. This distinction is a guaranteed board question and the first thing a practising CA checks.
c12_acc_ch04.subtitle: Rewrite the contract — or bury the company? Learn to tell which is which.
c12_acc_ch04.role: Legal advisor ruling on firm closures
c12_acc_ch04.intro: The word 'dissolution' hides two completely different events — and examiners bet you can't separate them.
c12_acc_ch04.goal: Distinguish dissolution of partnership from dissolution of firm and apply the legal modes of each.

discovery.question: A company offers shares paying a fixed 8% dividend, paid before anyone else, and refunded first on winding up — but holders cannot vote. What are these?
options: Preference shares — fixed dividend and priority in payment, but no voting rights
Equity shares — because every shareholder owns the company equally
Debentures — because the 8% return is fixed like interest
Sweat equity — issued for fixed consideration to employees
discovery.answer: Preference shares — fixed dividend and priority in payment, but no voting rights
discovery.hook: Fixed return tempts students to call it debt — but preference dividends come from profits, not contractual interest, and that single difference rewrites the balance sheet.

c12_acc_ch05.mission: Structure a ₹1 crore raise: weigh equity against preference capital, then choose between public issue, private placement and a rights issue — matching each route to the company's situation.
c12_acc_ch05.finale: You can now read a capital structure like an investor does. Equity vs preference and issue methods are board staples — and the actual vocabulary of every IPO headline you'll ever read.
c12_acc_ch05.subtitle: Fixed dividend or voting power? Every rupee of capital makes you choose.
c12_acc_ch05.role: CFO designing the company's share capital
c12_acc_ch05.intro: Raising ownership capital is a trade: what rights you sell decides what the money costs you.
c12_acc_ch05.goal: Compare equity and preference shares and select among public issue, private placement and rights issue.

discovery.question: Volt Motors needs ₹500 crore but refuses to dilute ownership or accept 12% bank covenants. Investors accept 10% instead. What did the company issue — and why did investors take less?
options: Secured debentures — lenders accept lower fixed interest because assets back the debt
Equity shares — investors always accept lower returns for voting rights
Preference shares — fixed dividend with ownership dilution
A bank overdraft — the cheapest form of long-term borrowing
discovery.answer: Secured debentures — lenders accept lower fixed interest because assets back the debt
discovery.hook: Students think lower return means worse deal — but security changes the risk, not just the rate. Debentures let a company borrow without surrendering a single vote.

c12_acc_ch06.mission: Structure a debenture issue: classify the instrument, then record it issued at par, premium and discount — tracing how each pricing choice moves cash, liabilities and reserves.
c12_acc_ch06.finale: Debt without dilution is a superpower — and you now know its price list. Debenture entries are pure board marks; understanding risk-vs-rate is pure investing wisdom.
c12_acc_ch06.subtitle: Borrow ₹500 crore without selling a single vote — welcome to debentures.
c12_acc_ch06.intro: The smartest companies grow on other people's money — debentures are the IOU that makes it possible.
c12_acc_ch06.goal: Classify debentures and journalise issue at par, premium and discount.

discovery.question: You open the annual reports of Reliance, TCS and a small unlisted company — and find the Balance Sheet laid out identically in all three. Who forces this uniformity?
options: Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013 — one prescribed format for every company
The company's auditor chooses the layout each year
SEBI dictates formats only to listed companies; others are free
Each board of directors designs its own Balance Sheet
discovery.answer: Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013 — one prescribed format for every company
discovery.hook: It feels like coincidence or convention — it's actually law. Schedule III standardises classification (current vs non-current, shareholders' funds vs liabilities) so any investor can compare any two companies.

c12_acc_ch07.mission: Build a company's Balance Sheet the Schedule III way: order the Equity & Liabilities blocks, split every item into current and non-current, and explain why the format exists at all.
c12_acc_ch07.finale: You can now navigate any Indian company's annual report without a guide. Schedule III formats are direct board marks — and the skeleton key to real financial analysis.
c12_acc_ch07.subtitle: Why does every Indian company's Balance Sheet look exactly the same?
c12_acc_ch07.intro: A company's financial statements aren't just records — they're a regulated language every business must speak identically.
c12_acc_ch07.goal: Apply Schedule III classification to prepare a compliant company Balance Sheet.

discovery.question: Two firms report identical current ratios of 2:1 — but one uses FIFO with straight-line depreciation, the other LIFO with written-down value. Can you say their liquidity is equal?
options: No — different accounting policies can manufacture identical ratios from very different realities
Yes — identical ratios always mean identical liquidity
Yes — ratio analysis eliminates all policy differences automatically
No — because LIFO is illegal under Indian accounting standards
discovery.answer: No — different accounting policies can manufacture identical ratios from very different realities
discovery.hook: Numbers feel objective; they're not. Analysis begins where blind trust ends — every statement rests on historical cost, policy choices and estimates that the raw ratio never reveals.

c12_acc_ch08.mission: Play the bank manager: take raw Balance Sheet and P&L data from a loan applicant, run the analysis, and stress-test your conclusion against the known limitations of financial statements.
c12_acc_ch08.finale: You now read statements like a lender — extracting signal while doubting the noise. Objective-and-limitation questions are board favourites; sceptical reading is a career skill.
c12_acc_ch08.subtitle: The ratio says 2:1. The truth says 'depends'. Learn the difference.
c12_acc_ch08.role: Credit analyst vetting a ₹50 lakh loan
c12_acc_ch08.intro: Financial statements are raw numbers until someone asks the right questions — that someone is the analyst.
c12_acc_ch08.goal: State the objectives of financial statement analysis and apply its limitations to real comparisons.

discovery.question: Your bakery's P&L shows ₹50,000 profit — yet your bank balance fell. Which statement explains the disappearance?
options: The Cash Flow Statement — it tracks actual cash, stripping out credit sales and non-cash items like depreciation
The Balance Sheet — it lists where every rupee went during the year
The P&L again — profit and cash are the same number if calculated correctly
The auditor's report — it reconciles profit to bank balance
discovery.answer: The Cash Flow Statement — it tracks actual cash, stripping out credit sales and non-cash items like depreciation
discovery.hook: Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact. Credit sales inflate profit without moving a rupee, and depreciation cuts profit without spending one — AS-3 exists to expose that gap.

c12_acc_ch09.mission: Reconcile profit to bank balance: classify movements into operating, investing and financing, then decide which near-cash items — 6-month FD, 45-day T-bills, blue-chip shares — qualify as cash equivalents.
c12_acc_ch09.finale: You can now answer the question that bankrupts profitable companies: where did the cash go? AS-3 classification is a guaranteed board question — and the core skill of every CFO.
c12_acc_ch09.subtitle: ₹50,000 profit, shrinking bank balance — solve the mystery of the missing cash.
c12_acc_ch09.intro: Companies don't die of losses — they die of empty bank accounts. This statement is the early-warning system.
c12_acc_ch09.goal: Define cash and cash equivalents per AS-3 and classify flows into operating, investing and financing.

discovery.question: A potato sprouts a new plant from an 'eye' while a mango needs flowers, pollen and seeds. What single feature truly separates these two modes of reproduction?
options: Whether gametes fuse — the potato clones itself through mitosis; the mango requires fertilisation between gametes
Whether a seed forms — everything producing seeds is sexual, everything else asexual
Whether two parents exist — sexual reproduction always needs two separate individuals
Whether the offspring looks different — identical offspring always mean asexual reproduction
discovery.answer: Whether gametes fuse — the potato clones itself through mitosis; the mango requires fertilisation between gametes
discovery.hook: Students count parents or look for seeds — the real boundary is gamete fusion, which is why a single organism can still reproduce sexually and identical-looking offspring can come from either mode.

c12_bio_ch01.mission: Sort a field of organisms — Amoeba, yeast in idli batter, Spirogyra, flowering plants — into their reproductive modes, then defend why variation matters more than speed for a species' future.
c12_bio_ch01.finale: You can now classify any reproduction you meet by its mechanism, not its looks. Asexual vs sexual anchoring is core board content — and the opening question of all evolutionary biology.
c12_bio_ch01.subtitle: A potato eye and a mango flower perform the same miracle by opposite logic.
c12_bio_ch01.intro: Life has exactly two ways to copy itself — and the difference decides whether a species survives change.
c12_bio_ch01.goal: Distinguish asexual from sexual reproduction by mechanism and evaluate the significance of each.

discovery.question: Tap a hibiscus anther over dark paper and yellow dust falls — pollen. Inside that anther, what actually produced each grain?
options: Microspore mother cells in the pollen sacs underwent meiosis to form haploid microspores
The stigma secreted pollen onto the anther during pollination
Petals shed cells that matured into pollen grains on the anther surface
Pollen mother cells divided by mitosis, keeping the diploid number
discovery.answer: Microspore mother cells in the pollen sacs underwent meiosis to form haploid microspores
discovery.hook: Pollen feels like powder, not biology — but each grain is a meiotic product carrying half the genome, made inside the anther's microsporangia long before any pollinator arrives.

c12_bio_ch02.mission: Dissect a flower layer by layer: identify all four whorls on the thalamus, slice a young anther to expose its four microsporangia, and trace pollen from meiosis to the stigma.
c12_bio_ch02.finale: You now see a flower as a reproductive machine, not decoration. Floral whorls and anther anatomy are board-diagram gold — and the foundation of every crop-breeding programme.
c12_bio_ch02.subtitle: Inside a hibiscus: four whorls, four pollen sacs, one precise machine.
c12_bio_ch02.intro: Every fruit you eat began as a flower executing a sequence older than humans — here's its blueprint.
c12_bio_ch02.goal: Identify floral whorls and trace microsporogenesis in the anther.

discovery.question: The testes sit outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum — a seemingly odd design. Why does sperm production demand it?
options: Spermatogenesis needs a temperature a few degrees below core body temperature
The scrotum protects testes from the pressure of the abdominal muscles
Sperm can only mature where oxygen concentration is highest
External placement allows the vas deferens to shorten its transport route
discovery.answer: Spermatogenesis needs a temperature a few degrees below core body temperature
discovery.hook: It looks like an anatomical accident; it's a thermal requirement. The scrotum is a cooling system — and the same logic explains undescended-testis infertility in clinical practice.

c12_bio_ch03.mission: Map both reproductive systems end-to-end: trace sperm from seminiferous tubules through the duct system, and ova from ovary through fimbriae to uterus — matching each structure to its function.
c12_bio_ch03.finale: You can now walk a gamete's entire journey in either system. Histology of testis and ovary is heavy board weightage — and the literal anatomy of fertility medicine.
c12_bio_ch03.subtitle: Why sperm needs a cooler room — and other design logic of human reproduction.
c12_bio_ch03.role: Medical student tracing the gamete's journey
c12_bio_ch03.intro: Every structure here exists because a gamete demanded it — anatomy is frozen function.
c12_bio_ch03.goal: Describe the anatomy and histology of male and female reproductive systems and their ducts.

discovery.question: A couple tells an ASHA worker: no pills, no surgery — but we want to plan our family. Which methods remain available to them?
options: Natural methods like periodic abstinence and lactational amenorrhoea, plus barriers like condoms
Nothing — effective contraception requires either drugs or devices
Only surgical options, since natural methods are unreliable by definition
Only hormone-free IUDs, which count as natural methods
discovery.answer: Natural methods like periodic abstinence and lactational amenorrhoea, plus barriers like condoms
discovery.hook: Students think contraception means intervention — but behavioural awareness and physical barriers prevent fertilisation without any drug, which is exactly why counselling starts with the full menu, not the prescription.

c12_bio_ch04.mission: Advise families across real scenarios: match natural, barrier and other contraceptive methods to each couple's needs, and connect reproductive health to its full WHO definition — physical, mental and social well-being.
c12_bio_ch04.finale: You now understand reproductive health as well-being, not just biology. Contraception comparison is board-critical — and this knowledge genuinely changes lives in public health.
c12_bio_ch04.subtitle: No pills, no surgery — can a family still be planned? Absolutely.
c12_bio_ch04.intro: Reproductive health is where biology meets real life — choices, dignity and well-being included.
c12_bio_ch04.goal: Define reproductive health per WHO and compare natural and barrier contraceptive methods.

discovery.question: Cross tall with dwarf peas and every F1 plant is tall — dwarfness vanishes. Self-pollinate the F1 and it returns at exactly 3:1. What was the dwarf trait doing in F1?
options: Present but masked — the recessive allele stayed intact, hidden by the dominant one
Destroyed — the dominant allele eliminated it permanently
Converted — the dwarf allele mutated into a tall allele
Blended — tall and dwarf merged into an intermediate that re-separated later
discovery.answer: Present but masked — the recessive allele stayed intact, hidden by the dominant one
discovery.hook: The blending intuition is deeply wrong: alleles are discrete units that segregate cleanly into gametes. The F2's precise 3:1 is the receipt proving nothing was lost or merged.

c12_bio_ch05.mission: Re-run Mendel's logic: predict F1 and F2 for a monohybrid cross, derive the 3:1 phenotypic and 1:2:1 genotypic ratios, and connect each law to what chromosomes physically do in meiosis.
c12_bio_ch05.finale: You now think in alleles, not appearances — the single biggest upgrade in genetics. Mendelian crosses are guaranteed board marks and the entry ticket to all of modern biology.
c12_bio_ch05.subtitle: The dwarf trait never left — it was hiding. Mendel proved inheritance has rules.
c12_bio_ch05.intro: One monk's garden arithmetic became the operating system of all heredity — here's the proof.
c12_bio_ch05.goal: Apply Mendel's laws to predict monohybrid cross outcomes and their ratios.

discovery.question: Hershey and Chase tagged a phage's DNA with ³²P and its protein with ³⁵S, then let it infect bacteria. Which label entered the cell — and what did that prove?
options: ³²P entered — DNA, not protein, is the genetic material passed to the next generation
³⁵S entered — protein carries the instructions for building new phages
Both entered — DNA and protein share the role of genetic material equally
Neither entered — the phage replicates entirely on the cell surface
discovery.answer: ³²P entered — DNA, not protein, is the genetic material passed to the next generation
discovery.hook: Protein was the favourite candidate — it seemed complex enough to carry information. Radioactive tracing settled it: only DNA crosses the cell wall, which is why the double helix matters at all.

c12_bio_ch06.mission: Reconstruct the evidence chain: follow Griffith's transforming principle through Hershey-Chase's radioactive verdict, then read the Watson-Crick double helix — antiparallel strands, A-T and G-C base pairs.
c12_bio_ch06.finale: You've just re-derived the most important conclusion in biology from raw evidence. Transformation, the helix and base-pairing are board heavyweights — and the foundation of all biotechnology.
c12_bio_ch06.subtitle: A radioactive label settled biology's biggest argument: DNA is the instruction book.
c12_bio_ch06.intro: Every gene edit and DNA test stands on two experiments and one elegant spiral staircase.
c12_bio_ch06.goal: Explain the evidence for DNA as genetic material and describe the double helix structure.
